newsitem.title: USA: PP&L postpones Susquehanna nuke restart.
newsitem.headline: PP&L postpones Susquehanna nuke restart.

text.p: Pennsylvania Power and Light Co (PP&L) said Wednesday the startup of the 1,090 megawatt (MW) Susquehanna 1 nuclear power unit, in Berwick, Pa., has been postponed for further maintenance work.
The unit was moving into a cold shutdown mode as of early Wednesday, postponing a resumption of power production that had been planned for today, a company spokeswoman said.
"We had been planning to bring it up today, but our concern is to get it fixed properly before we restart it," the spokeswoman said.
No new restart date for the unit has yet been set, she said.

Susquehanna 1 was taken off line Feb 25 in anticipation of a loss of vacuum in the unit's main condenser. A restart of the unit was later delayed for additional work on a residual heat removal system.
The unit was placed in a restart mode earlier this week, but that restart was postponed by the further maintenance work.

The adjoining Susquehanna unit 2, with a capacity of 1,094 MW, was operating at 87 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday as it coasted down to a refueling and maintenance shutdown scheduled to begin March 15, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission said in its daily plant status report.
